interpretation_keys.fish_alone_already_at_sm_92pct: Fish standalone is itself SM-bound; little headroom exists for any cohabitant.
interpretation_keys.vllm_pushes_sm_to_97pct_but_memutil_DROP: Pattern (SM up, mem util down, power down) is classic scheduling/SM-contention — kernels stall waiting for SMs, idle on the bus and consuming less HBM bandwidth.
interpretation_keys.ttfb_unchanged: Fish HTTP server stays sub-5ms TTFB across all conditions — bottleneck is wall-clock to render, not first-byte latency.
interpretation_keys.no_oom_no_throttle: FB stayed 88-90 GB / 274 GB total. mclk pinned at 3996 MHz. pviol/tviol = 0. No HBM saturation, no thermal/power throttle.
interpretation_keys.single_cuda_context_no_mps: All four PIDs (Parakeet 173799, Fish 217878, vLLM 285669/285796, support 236296) share GPU 0 with no MPS partition — every kernel funnels through the same default-priority CUDA stream pool.

nsys_skip_reason: nsys 2024.6.2 supports launch-only profiling; would require restarting Fish under nsys wrapper. Restart violates the 'no architectural changes' constraint. SM/mem/power telemetry alone is sufficient to infer the bottleneck class with this magnitude of effect.
verdict: scheduling (SM-contention) — NOT HBM-bandwidth, NOT compute-saturation per se
verdict_justification: Fish standalone already runs at 92% SM util on B300 — it is itself compute-heavy.

Adding vLLM raises SM util only +5pp (92->97) but kills Fish throughput by 78%. If both kernels were truly running in parallel we'd see SM saturate near 100% with mem util ALSO climbing; instead mem util DROPS from 33% to 24% and power drops from 530W to 463W.

That signature (SM% high, mem util AND power both fall) is the canonical fingerprint of CUDA stream serialization — the SM scheduler is rotating between the two contexts; while one waits the other is stalled, so HBM gets less work.
HBM bandwidth is NOT the bottleneck: 8 TB/s aggregate, only ~24-34% mem util observed. There are 184 GB free VRAM; no eviction.

Compute alone is NOT the bottleneck either: Fish-alone p95 RTF 1.97 already represents the pure-compute ceiling on the current S2-Pro PyTorch graph; the +95% degradation under all-busy is purely contention-induced.

Parakeet-only adds just +11% RTF: confirms vLLM is the dominant noise source, not Parakeet. vLLM's 30B-A3B MoE constantly issues large GEMMs that occupy SMs for long bursts and starve Fish's smaller kernels.

ooda_top_action.primary: Enable CUDA MPS with stream-priority hints; assign Fish HIGH priority and vLLM DEFAULT. MPS partitions SMs at the kernel-scheduler level instead of round-robin context-switching, which is exactly what removes the observed 'SM% up, mem util down' fingerprint.
ooda_top_action.secondary: Re-pin vLLM's --gpu-memory-utilization (currently 0.20 with --max-num-seqs 8, --kv-cache-dtype fp8) to free a fixed SM budget for Fish — vLLM's --num-scheduler-steps and --cuda-graph-sizes can be tuned to reduce kernel granularity, giving Fish more interleave windows.
ooda_top_action.tertiary: If MPS+priority insufficient, the next lever is moving Fish's text2semantic to a separate CUDA stream with cudaStreamCreateWithPriority and submitting in a torch.cuda.stream() block. This is a Fish-side change, not a service-restart issue.
ooda_top_action.do_not_do: Quantizing Fish or moving its KV cache off-card. HBM is not the bottleneck — there's 184 GB free and mem util is 24-34%. Optimizing what isn't broken would burn time and possibly hurt latency.
